content:
Ready for a full Class 4 Maths Olympiad rehearsal? A real IMO or SOF paper mixes every chapter — numbers, factors, fractions, decimals, money, measurement, time, geometry, perimeter and area, patterns and data handling — in one 30-question set. This free test gives a 10-question taste, and the practice-papers e-book gives you 25 complete Maths Olympiad Class 4 sample papers with answers.

What a Class 4 IMO sample paper looks like

  • 30 questions in one paper, balanced across all 11 chapters
  • A mix of number work, factors, fractions, decimals, money, measurement, time, geometry and data
  • An answer key and step-by-step solution for every question
  • Graded intermediate to hard, just like the real SOF Olympiad

How to use Class 4 Olympiad practice papers

  • Sit one paper in a quiet 30–40 minute slot, no help
  • Mark it with the answer key, then read the solution for every wrong one
  • Note which chapter the mistakes cluster in and revise that chapter
  • Repeat weekly — steady practice beats last-minute cramming

Take the free mixed test

quiz.intro: Ten questions from across the syllabus. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 4: all chapters

questions.q: A newspaper prints the crowd of 2,64,718 rounded to the nearest 1,000. Which number appears?
questions.explanation: 2,64,718 lies between 2,64,000 and 2,65,000; it is nearer to 2,65,000, so it rounds to 2,65,000.

questions.q: Mira claims all of 60, 84, 106, 132 are multiples of 12. Which number proves her wrong?
questions.explanation: 60 = 12 × 5, 84 = 12 × 7, 132 = 12 × 11, but 106 ÷ 12 = 8 remainder 10, so 106 is not a multiple of 12.

questions.q: 4 2/5 is the same as which improper fraction?
questions.explanation: Multiply the whole part by the denominator and add the numerator: 4 x 5 + 2 = 22, so 4 2/5 = 22/5.

questions.q: In which place does the digit 5 sit in 61.58, and what is its value?
questions.explanation: 5 is the first digit after the decimal point, so it is in the tenths place with value 0.5.

questions.q: Meera buys 6 notebooks priced at Rs 24 each. How much does she pay in all?
questions.explanation: Cost of 6 items = Rs 24 x 6 = Rs 144.

questions.q: A jogging loop in a park is 250 m around. How many rounds make 1 km 500 m?

questions.q: Tara counts down from 100 in steps of 8: 100, 92, 84, … Which of these numbers will she say?
questions.explanation: Every number said differs from 100 by a multiple of 8; 100 − 8 × 6 = 52, so 52 is said.
